lots.what_it_is: Box of 13 Sega games: 11 Mega Drive/Genesis (PGA Tour 96 and PGA Tour Golf II in US Genesis cases, The Smurfs, a soccer cart probably FIFA International Soccer, NBA Jam, The Chaos Engine, NHL 96, Shaq-Fu, Sonic the Hedgehog, The Lion King, The Terminator) and 2 Master System (California Games, Alex Kidd in Shinobi World). Common titles; Alex Kidd and Chaos Engine are the better ones.
lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo; 13 items counted (researcher said about 12 and missed NBA Jam, Shaq-Fu and the soccer cart). Both PGA cases are US Sega Genesis issues ('Licensed by Sega Enterprises Ltd. for play on the SEGA GENESIS SYSTEM' read on crops), so possibly NTSC carts, contents not visible. The Chaos Engine label has a large torn patch (paper missing over the left half of the art) which badly hurts its value. Sonic and Shaq-Fu labels worn or stained. Smurfs, NBA Jam, Terminator, Lion King, NHL 96 and Chaos Engine show Mega Drive branding (PAL). Two SMS carts have red grid Sega labels, readable.
lots.condition: Loose carts with label wear; Chaos Engine label torn; Sonic and NBA Jam labels scuffed; two cased Genesis games with case wear. Working order unknown.

lots.guide_summary: SOLD evidence is single-title eBay sales on PriceCharting, all pages opened. Sum of the low recent sale per title (Chaos Engine halved for its torn label) is about AUD 128; PriceCharting guide sum (ASKING-type, undamaged copies) is about AUD 210. lots.working: Per-title low recent SOLD in AUD (1.4352): Chaos Engine 35.06 x 0.5 for torn label = 17.53 (my condition discount), Alex Kidd 20.65, Smurfs 19.40, NBA Jam 8.90, Terminator 7.51, NHL 96 10.98, Sonic 4.85, Lion King 5.65, Shaq Fu 7.97, California Games 8.41, FIFA 7.51, PGA Tour 96 8.87, PGA Tour Golf II 13.13 = AUD 141.36; using the Smurfs older low (9.63 = 13.82) and PGA96 low CIB (3.49 = 5.01) and PGA II (6.18 = 8.87) brings it to about AUD 127.66. keep_max = 127.66 / 1.198 = 106.56, round down to $105 (all-in $125.79). This is a component sum, not a single same-lot sale. Flip: piecemeal resale mid about AUD 178, less eBay fees 13.4% (AUD 23.85) and postage/packing subsidy about AUD 2 x 13 = AUD 26, net about AUD 128; / 2.396 = 53.42, round down to $50. Pickup Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Most titles read in the photo and matching SOLD entries opened for every title, but they are individual eBay sales, the soccer cart title is inferred, Genesis case contents are unknown and nothing is tested.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's Chaos Engine 'approx 24-27 multiple Aug 2026' figure: those PriceCharting rows are a repeated dealer listing titled 'CHAOS ENGINE 2', not this game, and the researcher assumed the currency; replaced with the genuine Chaos Engine cart-only sales (US$24.43 2026-06-09, US$45.15 2025-11-15), filed as close because the lot label is torn. Dropped the PAL Mega Drive PGA Tour Golf II entry (US$4.23 and a 'complete 3.30' I could not find on the page): the lot copy is a US Genesis case, so I used the Sega Genesis page instead. Dropped the Lion King entry because its AUD figure was the guide price filed as SOLD; replaced with actual sales. Currency is USD (confirmed on page), not 'assumed'; rate corrected from 1.50 to 1.4352.
lots.question_for_gowans: Do the two PGA Genesis cases contain carts, and are they US (NTSC) Genesis carts? What is the soccer cart's title? Has anything been tested? Note the Chaos Engine label is torn.

lots.key_photo_findings: Single photo. Corgi box code '05301' read on the box front, 'Detailed scale model for the adult collector' header; car with figures visible in window, looks complete. Matchbox box reads 'THUNDERBIRDS RESCUE PACK' and '54321 THUNDERBI...'. Sticker read on enlarged crop: 'T/BIRD RESCUE PACK, QTY: 1, CAT PRICE £22.99, R0209 12 RY99' with barcode, i.e. old UK catalogue-shop stock; not a market value. Contents of the Thunderbirds box are not shown and it is unclear whether it is sealed.

lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so no maximum bid. Both are common 1990s releases; value unverified.
